requests.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original Victoria 3 BUILDING icon for regional land-transport infrastructure, not a goods cutout and not a production-method glyph. Paint a compact elevated three-quarter view of a late-eighteenth/early-nineteenth-century road interchange around a modest masonry coaching inn with stable yard, a little arched stone bridge and a wooden toll gate. Clear road connection between structures; large readable architecture, limited tiny details. This building represents a network, not only a railway station: no train, rails or modern vehicles in this initial road-based visual. A single large traditional four-wheel wooden passenger carriage is the functional symbol in the lower-right foreground, with cream upper body, dark red lower coach body, brown spoked wheels and visible undercarriage; stationary in the yard, no horses needed for this symbol. Keep the carriage large and clear, without covering the main bridge or inn. Darken ONLY the scene behind the foreground coach using natural local shadows so the coach stands out; preserve natural warm stone, brown wood, muted green foliage and neutral lighting elsewhere, no overall blue or sepia cast. Hand-painted stylized historical game art with visible broad brush texture, not photorealism. Include the thin patinated metal rounded-square frame characteristic of Victoria 3 BUILDING icons, complete and uncut. Fill the frame with the small scene, genuine transparent alpha only outside its rounded corners and perimeter; no black padding baked into the art. Square master at least 1024 pixels, entire coach and frame visible, opaque interior scene (not translucent). No readable text, number, sign lettering, flags, logo, watermark, glowing border or interface elements. Original illustrative transport hub, not a certified reconstruction or direct copy of a photograph.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: single Victoria 3 TECHNOLOGY icon for early-nineteenth-century engineered roads. Show one compact physical cutaway SAMPLE of a raised cambered road, with an earthy foundation, visible large interlocking foundation stones, a finer compacted aggregate layer on top and slightly lowered drainage channels at the sides. A short wooden-handled iron hand tamper rests diagonally against the sample as the only accessory. The broad stone layers are the dominant subject. Inspired by the documented Telford system of drainage and graded stones, not an exact dimensioned engineering diagram. No cobblestone street scene, bitumen/asphalt coating, modern road markings, vehicle, landscaped terrain, people or bridge. Three-quarter slightly elevated view; isolated object group, entire sample and hand tamper visible with small transparent margins. Hand-painted volumetric Victoria 3 technology-art style with matte natural warm gray limestone, brown earth, oak handle and dark gray iron; broad brushwork, restrained highlights, NOT uniform gold monochrome like a PM, no overall blue or sepia tint. Square master at least 1024 pixels. Genuine transparent alpha background and gaps, all four corners exactly transparent. No frame, medallion, badge, background disc, tabletop, floor, readable text, labels, numbers, arrows, logo, watermark, glow or photorealistic rendering.

Dirt ruts must distinguish this from a smooth stone engineered road; no loose pebble pile, stone pavement, toll gate or tar. Keep the wheel complete and the road as a small isolated symbol, not a landscape. Restrained ochre-gold bas-relief palette consistent with the road PM series.
